what: Is a census run bit for bit itself across processes on one card? A calib_rel run of 16 neurons and 8 controls at layer 45 (868 answers, --batch 64 --max-new 64 --unpacker compiled) on the home RTX 5090, 29 October 2026, 00:32-00:37 CDT, at commit 221b698 (the tree not clean). Quoted in ROADMAP §vi (the census on larger and rented cards).

result.unbroken_vs_merged: the run taken unbroken and the same run taken in two shards and merged (census_tools.py merge) are the same file: 868 rows, every one of their 17 fields equal, the bytes identical (sha256 50f16b89...)
result.canaries: the canary batch (plan batch 0, 64 answers) written in two separate processes (CANA, CANB) and again by shard 1 for the merge are identical, every field of every row (sha256 4a6b0f18...); the merge's own record says 'identical on 1 of 1 shard'
result.not_measured: how far a run differs across cards

how.run_det.sh: the script as it ran, kept as it is. Its second shard was asked for as --shard 2/2, which census_run.py refuses (logs/s2.log: shards count from 0); shard 0 of 2 was then run by hand with the same arguments (logs/s0.log), and the two merged by census_tools.py merge (no log kept; the merged meta is metas/sharded.DET.meta.json).
how.compare.py: reads the kept runs and writes compare.json: rows, fields, rows differing, bytes and sha256 of each pair, and the sha256 of every kept file (CPU only)

files.logs/: unbroken.log, s1.log (shard 1 of 2, with its canary), s2.log (the refused 2/2), s0.log (shard 0 of 2), ca.log and cb.log (the two canaries)
files.metas/: each run's meta and each canary's settings, as written
files.runs: atlas_data/offline/census_determinism/ (gitignored): census/ (the unbroken run DET.jsonl, 5.6 MB, and the canaries CANA, CANB) and sharded/ (both shards, shard 1's canary and the merged DET.jsonl); compare.json gives every file's sha256
